author: CC
prose: Hypotheses, unmeasured, offered in conversation with Akien 2026-11-23 on his 'specialized areas, local reads' idea. (1) The partition rule is: cut where traffic is thinnest — dense wiring inside an area, sparse summaries between areas, as in the brain and in a layer-split LLM. (2) Each area owns its state (Law 6) and serves its own reads from local memory; only votes or summaries cross the bus. (3) A column's working memory is in-process, not a DB call; the DB is the durable record, written behind in batches or snapshots — remove the steps rather than speed the call. (4) Cognition can be asynchronous: each area runs on its own clock and acts on the latest votes, tolerating staleness, so inter-area latency need not multiply per step the way it does in LLM decoding. (5) Gains flatten as partitions multiply, so areas should be few and coarse. First measurements: one DB call's latency through the proxy today; in a small simulation, reads per column per tick and the fraction that would cross an area boundary under a given split.
